name: Chronicle AI history dataset
description: 106 milestones in the history of artificial intelligence from 1943 to 2026, each dated, categorized, scored for significance under a published rubric and linked to its primary source.
attribution: Chronicle AI history dataset (https://epoch.founden.co/data), CC BY 4.0

fields.description: Stable identifier of the event, also its dossier slug.
When it happened: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY when only the year is established.
Calendar year.
day, month or year: how precisely the date is known.
The subject as people name and search for it, for example Turing test.
Editorial headline.
The person, lab or institution behind it.
Models, Research, Launches, Open source, Benchmarks, Policy, Culture or Robotics.
What happened, in one sentence.
Why it mattered, in one sentence.
Editorial significance from 0 to 100: the weighted sum of the 5 ratings under rubric 1.0.
Defining (80 to 100), Major (60 to 79) or Notable (0 to 59).
Established, Supported or Provisional: how settled the evidence and historical perspective are. It does not change the score.
Conceptual shift, 0 to 5, worth 30% of the score: How much did this change the available approach?
Downstream influence, 0 to 5, worth 25% of the score: How much subsequent research or practice does it underpin?
Breadth of impact, 0 to 5, worth 20% of the score: How widely did the change matter beyond its original setting?
Access & diffusion, 0 to 5, worth 15% of the score: How much did it enable others to use or build on the work?
Institutional change, 0 to 5, worth 10% of the score: Did it change lasting infrastructure, governance, or incentives?
The original paper, announcement or archive record.
Sources cited in the event's dossier.
The event's full, cited dossier.

events.name: McCulloch-Pitts neuron
events.title: A mathematical neuron
events.summary: McCulloch and Pitts prove that networks of all-or-none threshold neurons are equivalent to formal logic.
events.impact: Von Neumann used their notation for the EDVAC design, and Kleene built finite automata theory on it.

events.name: Turing test
events.title: The question that started it all
events.summary: Turing swaps "Can machines think?" for the imitation game, in which an interrogator judges typed replies.
events.impact: It gave AI a shared, testable question that ELIZA, Searle and 2025 language model trials all returned to.

events.name: Logic Theorist
events.title: Rules of thumb prove theorems
events.summary: Newell, Shaw and Simon's program proves 38 of 52 Principia theorems by heuristic search, not enumeration.
events.impact: Its selective search over symbol lists led to IPL list processing, the General Problem Solver and symbolic AI.

events.name: Dartmouth workshop
events.title: Artificial intelligence gets a name
events.summary: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon name artificial intelligence and gather its founders at Dartmouth.
events.impact: The name and its conjecture became the banner for AI labs, departments, journals and funding lines.

events.name: Perceptron
events.title: The perceptron
events.summary: Rosenblatt's perceptron learns to classify patterns by adjusting its connection weights from labeled examples.
events.impact: Learning weights from errors became a running procedure, the principle backpropagation later extended.

events.name: LISP
events.title: Programs become data
events.summary: McCarthy begins LISP at MIT: recursive functions over lists, with programs written as the same lists they process.
events.impact: It became the main language of US AI research for three decades and the basis of the 1980s Lisp machine industry.

events.name: Arthur Samuel's checkers program
events.title: Learning from a game of checkers
events.summary: Samuel's IBM 701 checkers program improves by tuning its own position-scoring weights through self-play.
events.impact: Its rule of nudging an estimate toward a later one became temporal-difference learning.

events.name: Unimate
events.title: A programmable arm joins the line
events.summary: Unimation's Unimate, a teach-and-replay hydraulic arm, starts unloading die castings at a GM plant in New Jersey.
events.impact: It made the reprogrammable arm a product, seeding an industry with 5 million factory robots in use by 2025.

events.name: DENDRAL expert system
events.title: Expertise becomes software
events.summary: DENDRAL proposes and ranks organic molecule structures from a mass spectrum using encoded chemical rules.
events.impact: Its lesson that knowledge beats general method spawned MYCIN and the 1980s expert systems industry.

events.name: ELIZA chatbot
events.title: A conversation with ELIZA
events.summary: Weizenbaum's ELIZA mimics a Rogerian therapist by matching keywords and reflecting users' own words back.
events.impact: People read empathy into it, naming the ELIZA effect and turning Weizenbaum into a lifelong AI critic.

events.name: Shakey the robot
events.title: Shakey enters the world
events.summary: SRI begins Shakey, a camera-equipped robot that perceives rooms, plans actions in logic and pushes boxes.
events.impact: The project left A* search, the STRIPS planner and the Hough line detector, all still in use.

events.name: Perceptrons (Minsky and Papert)
events.title: What one layer cannot compute
events.summary: Minsky and Papert prove one-layer perceptrons with local detectors cannot compute parity or connectedness.
events.impact: Its theorems, and a guess that many layers were sterile, cast neural nets as a dead end until the 1980s revival.

events.name: SHRDLU
events.title: Understanding inside a world of blocks
events.summary: Terry Winograd's SHRDLU parses typed English, resolves pronouns and moves blocks in a simulated tabletop world.
events.impact: Lighthill hailed it as exceptional yet doubted it could scale; its pronoun puzzle became the Winograd schema.

events.name: First AI winter
events.title: The first AI winter
events.summary: Lighthill's report to Britain's Science Research Council finds AI's general ambitions have delivered little.
events.impact: Britain withdrew support from most AI groups, part of a 1974 to 1980 contraction on 2 continents.

events.name: MYCIN expert system
events.title: A consultant built from rules
events.summary: Shortliffe's MYCIN chains 200 if-then rules backward to pick antibiotics and can explain why it asks each question.
events.impact: Its engine, stripped of medicine, became EMYCIN for other fields, but MYCIN itself never reached a hospital ward.

events.name: XCON (R1) expert system
events.title: Expert systems go into production
events.summary: DEC puts McDermott's R1 (XCON), a 772-rule system, to work configuring VAX-11/780 computer orders.
events.impact: The expert-system boom's showcase grew to 6,200 rules, half changed yearly, exposing the cost of upkeep.

events.name: Neocognitron
events.title: Shift invariance built into the wiring
events.summary: Fukushima's NHK network alternates learned S-cell and fixed C-cell layers to recognize patterns wherever they sit.
events.impact: Its shared-weight and pooling layers become the layout that LeNet and AlexNet later train by backpropagation.

events.name: Hopfield network
events.title: Memory as an energy landscape
events.summary: John Hopfield shows a symmetric network of binary units stores memories as stable states it settles into.
events.impact: It gave recurrent networks a provable energy function and drew physicists into neural network research.

events.name: Fifth Generation Computer Systems project
events.title: Japan bets a decade on logic machines
events.summary: Japan's MITI founds ICOT to build parallel logic-programming machines for knowledge processing over ten years.
events.impact: It spurred Britain's Alvey and rival programs; its parallel machines met speed goals but never found a market.

events.name: Backpropagation
events.title: Learning by backpropagation
events.summary: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams show in Nature that backpropagated errors let hidden units learn their own features.
events.impact: Its two-pass gradient procedure still trains nearly every deployed neural network.

events.name: Second AI winter
events.title: The boom meets its balance sheet
events.summary: Lisp machine makers and expert-system startups slide into loss as a skeptic takes over DARPA's AI funding.
events.impact: DARPA's AI and robotics budget fell over a third by 1989, and AAAI membership shrank from its 1987 peak of 16,421.

events.name: Bayesian networks
events.title: Uncertainty gets a calculus
events.summary: Judea Pearl's 1988 book makes graphs of local probabilities, updated by passed messages, AI's tool for uncertainty.
events.impact: Graphical models displace expert-system certainty factors and later drive turbo decoding, spam filters, causal AI.

events.name: LeNet (convolutional networks)
events.title: Learned filters read the mail
events.summary: LeCun's Bell Labs team trains a shared-weight convolutional network end to end on 7,291 real zip code digits.
events.impact: Learned filters replace hand-built ones; the line reads millions of checks a day by 1998 and leads to AlexNet.

events.name: Q-learning
events.title: Learning what an action is worth
events.summary: Christopher Watkins' Cambridge thesis defines Q-learning, which learns optimal action values without a model.
events.impact: Off-policy action values become the core of value-based RL, from Q-routing to DQN playing Atari from pixels.

events.name: TD-Gammon
events.title: Learning backgammon from its own games
events.summary: IBM's TD-Gammon learns backgammon from games against itself, then loses just 7 points in 38 games to top players.
events.impact: Its rollouts overturn expert opening play, and its self-play value network becomes a template DQN and AlphaGo cite.

events.name: Support vector machines
events.title: The widest margin wins
events.summary: Cortes and Vapnik add slack to the maximum-margin kernel classifier, tying LeNet-4 at 1.1% error on NIST digits.
events.impact: Convex, theory-backed kernel classifiers became machine learning's default tool until deep networks overtook them.

events.name: Deep Blue vs Kasparov
events.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
events.summary: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world champion Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5 in a six-game match in New York.
events.impact: It ended chess as AI's frontier benchmark, pushing the question to language and perception.

events.name: LSTM
events.title: Neural networks learn to remember
events.summary: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's gated memory cell lets a recurrent network learn across lags of over 1000 steps.
events.impact: Gated memory powered speech recognition and Google's production translation until the Transformer displaced it.

events.name: Random forests
events.title: Strength from uncorrelated trees
events.summary: Breiman grows unpruned trees on bootstrap samples, each split weighing a few random features, and lets them vote.
events.impact: A fast, nearly tuning-free default for tabular data, and one of the 25 most-cited papers published since 2000.

events.name: Neural probabilistic language model
events.title: Words become learned representations
events.summary: Bengio's team learns a vector per word while predicting the next word, beating smoothed n-gram models.
events.impact: Learned embeddings became the basic unit of neural NLP, reused by word2vec and GloVe.

events.name: DARPA Grand Challenge
events.title: Driverless across the desert
events.summary: Stanford's robot Stanley wins DARPA's 132-mile desert race in 6 h 54 min, one of five finishers among 23 starters.
events.impact: Its veterans staffed Google's self-driving project, and DARPA made prize challenges a standing research tool.

events.name: Deep belief networks
events.title: The deep learning revival
events.summary: Hinton, Osindero and Teh train a deep network one RBM layer at a time, reaching 1.25% error on MNIST digits.
events.impact: Layer-wise pretraining made deep networks credible again, leading to deep speech recognition by 2012.

events.name: NVIDIA CUDA
events.title: GPUs become programmable compute
events.summary: NVIDIA posts a public beta of its CUDA C compiler and SDK, letting developers program GPUs directly in C.
events.impact: It made GPUs the practical substrate for deep learning, from AlexNet's 2012 win to the cuDNN library.

events.name: ImageNet
events.title: ImageNet changes the dataset
events.summary: Deng, Fei-Fei and Princeton colleagues release ImageNet: 3.2 million verified images in 5,247 WordNet categories.
events.impact: Its 1,000-class challenge became computer vision's shared yardstick, where deep learning won in 2012.

events.name: IBM Watson
events.title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
events.summary: IBM's Watson beats Jeopardy! champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter, winning $77,147 to $24,000 and $21,600.
events.impact: It made machine question answering legible to a mass audience, then got oversold into cancer care.

events.name: AlexNet
events.title: AlexNet transforms image recognition
events.summary: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton's GPU-trained convolutional network wins ImageNet 2012 with 15.3% top-5 error.
events.impact: An 11-point margin over hand-engineered features turns computer vision toward learned features and GPU training.

events.name: word2vec
events.title: Word relationships in vector space
events.summary: Mikolov's Google team shows two shallow models learn word vectors from 1.6 billion words in under a day.
events.impact: Free pretrained vectors make embeddings the default first layer of neural NLP until contextual models arrive.

events.name: Deep Q-network
events.title: Learning to play from pixels
events.summary: DeepMind's Q-network learns 7 Atari games from raw pixels with one recipe, beating prior methods on 6.
events.impact: Deep reinforcement learning becomes a research program, as Double DQN, A3C and Rainbow refine its recipe.

events.name: Variational autoencoder
events.title: Learning a generative latent space
events.summary: Kingma and Welling backpropagate through random sampling to train a generative autoencoder.
events.impact: It becomes a standard generative component, from beta-VAE and VQ-VAE to Stable Diffusion's latent space.

events.name: Generative adversarial networks
events.title: Machines learn to imagine
events.summary: Goodfellow's Montreal team trains a generator by pitting it against a discriminator network.
events.impact: GANs carry image synthesis to photoreal StyleGAN faces by 2018, before diffusion overtakes them.

events.name: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio)
events.title: Learning where to look
events.organization: Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio · Université de Montréal
events.summary: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio's RNNsearch weights all source words afresh for each output word, not one fixed vector.
events.impact: Soft attention spreads to captioning, speech and production translation, then becomes the Transformer's core.

events.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
events.title: One sequence becomes another
events.summary: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le's LSTM ensemble out-translates a phrase-based system, 34.81 to 33.30 BLEU.
events.impact: The encoder-decoder becomes a reusable interface, from image captions to the Transformer.

events.name: Adam optimizer
events.title: Adam changes the training toolkit
events.summary: Kingma and Ba's Adam gives every parameter its own step size from bias-corrected gradient moment estimates.
events.impact: Adam and its AdamW variant become the standard optimizer for Transformers and large language models.

events.name: ResNet
events.title: Depth without the degradation
events.summary: Microsoft's He, Zhang, Ren and Sun train 152-layer residual networks and win ImageNet 2015 at 3.57% top-5 error.
events.impact: Skip connections become a default, wrapping every Transformer sub-layer that language models inherit.

events.name: OpenAI
events.title: OpenAI is founded
events.summary: Altman, Musk, Brockman and Sutskever launch OpenAI, a nonprofit AI lab with $1 billion in pledged funding.
events.impact: A funded nonprofit rival draws talent from corporate labs and makes AGI governance a mainstream question.

events.name: AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol
events.title: Move 37. A new kind of intuition.
events.summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol 4 to 1 at Go in Seoul, with the startling Move 37 in game two.
events.impact: Learned evaluation plus search cracks Go and launches the AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero and MuZero line.

events.name: Google Neural Machine Translation
events.title: Phrase tables give way to neural networks
events.summary: Google moves all Chinese to English in Translate, about 18 million translations a day, to a deep LSTM network.
events.impact: Translate goes neural for 16 directions by November, and its wordpieces pass to the Transformer and BERT.

events.name: Transformer
events.title: Attention is all you need
events.summary: Eight researchers unveil the Transformer, an attention-only model scoring 28.4 BLEU on English-German translation.
events.impact: Its attention-only design becomes the base of BERT, T5, GPT-3 and the Vision Transformer.

events.name: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences (RLHF)
events.title: A reward learned from human choices
events.summary: OpenAI and DeepMind agents learn from rewards fit to human clip comparisons, a backflip from 900 judgments.
events.impact: Reward models fit to human comparisons become RLHF, the tuning step behind InstructGPT and ChatGPT.

events.name: AlphaZero
events.title: Mastery through self-play
events.summary: One DeepMind algorithm learns chess, shogi and Go from the rules alone and beats the top program in each.
events.impact: A single self-play recipe displaces three hand-built engine traditions and seeds MuZero and AlphaTensor.

events.name: GPT-1
events.title: The first GPT
events.summary: OpenAI pretrains a Transformer decoder on 7,000 books, then fine-tunes it to records on 9 of 12 language tasks.
events.impact: Pretrain on raw text, then adapt becomes the recipe that GPT-2 and GPT-3 scale up.

events.name: BERT
events.title: BERT reads both ways
events.summary: Google's BERT learns by predicting masked words from both sides, setting records on 11 language tasks.
events.impact: Within a year Google applies it to about 1 in 10 US English searches, and RoBERTa and DistilBERT build on it.

events.name: GPT-2
events.title: GPT-2 and the release debate
events.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-2, a 1.5 billion parameter language model, but withholds its full weights over misuse risk.
events.impact: Its prompt-as-task recipe scales into GPT-3, and staged release becomes a lasting term in launch policy.

events.name: T5
events.title: Every language task is text-to-text
events.summary: Google's T5 frames every language task as text in, text out, and releases the 750 GB C4 corpus with its models.
events.impact: The text-to-text format and C4 become reused defaults, underpinning mT5, T0, UL2 and Flan-T5.

events.name: Scaling laws for neural language models
events.title: Bigger models, predictably better
events.summary: Kaplan's OpenAI team finds language-model loss falls as power laws in parameters, data and compute.
events.impact: Labs start sizing models by extrapolation; GPT-3 follows its big-model advice until Chinchilla revises it.

events.name: GPT-3
events.title: GPT-3 scales up
events.summary: OpenAI's 175 billion parameter GPT-3 performs many language tasks from a few examples in its prompt.
events.impact: Prompting one hosted model becomes an alternative to per-task fine-tuning, and metered API access a template.

events.name: DDPM
events.title: Learning to reverse noise
events.summary: Berkeley's Ho, Jain and Abbeel train an image model to reverse noise, reaching a record 3.17 FID on CIFAR-10.
events.impact: Diffusion becomes competitive with GANs, leading to guidance, latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion.

events.name: Waymo fully driverless public service
events.title: The driver's seat goes empty
events.summary: Waymo opens rides with no one behind the wheel to Waymo One riders across about 50 square miles of metro Phoenix.
events.impact: Paid public robotaxi rides without a safety driver begin, growing to over 400,000 rides a week by 2026.

events.name: Vision Transformer
events.title: Images become patch sequences
events.summary: Dosovitskiy's Google team runs a plain Transformer on 16x16 image patches and reaches 88.55% on ImageNet.
events.impact: Images and text come to share one architecture, the base for Swin, DINO, MAE and CLIP's image encoder.

events.name: AlphaFold 2
events.title: A 50-year biology problem
events.summary: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicts unseen protein structures at CASP14 with a median score of 92.4 GDT.
events.impact: Blind structure prediction nears lab accuracy, and over 200 million predicted structures are public by 2022.

events.name: DALL·E
events.title: DALL·E: language becomes image
events.summary: OpenAI's DALL·E, a 12-billion-parameter transformer, draws images from captions such as an avocado armchair.
events.impact: A typed sentence becomes the control for image generation, though diffusion replaces its method by 2022.

events.name: GitHub Copilot
events.title: Your AI pair programmer
events.summary: GitHub previews Copilot, an editor extension in which OpenAI's Codex suggests whole lines and functions.
events.impact: Code generation becomes a daily paid tool, and its security and licensing questions turn concrete.

events.name: Latent diffusion models
events.title: Diffusion leaves pixel space
events.summary: Rombach's Munich team runs image diffusion in an autoencoder's compressed latent space, not raw pixels.
events.impact: Diffusion gets cheap enough to release openly: the design ships as Stable Diffusion in 2022.

events.name: InstructGPT
events.title: Learning what users prefer
events.summary: Labelers prefer OpenAI's 1.3-billion-parameter InstructGPT, tuned on human feedback, to 175-billion GPT-3.
events.impact: Preference tuning becomes the standard post-training stage, and ChatGPT applies it to dialogue.

events.name: Chinchilla scaling laws
events.title: Scale the data, not just the model
events.summary: DeepMind's 70B Chinchilla, trained on 1.4 trillion tokens, beats the 280B Gopher at equal compute.
events.impact: Training data comes to scale with model size, near 20 tokens per parameter, paving the way for LLaMA.

events.name: DALL·E 2
events.title: DALL·E 2
events.summary: OpenAI's DALL·E 2 generates and edits 1024x1024 images by decoding CLIP embeddings with diffusion.
events.impact: Text-to-image becomes an editing tool for non-specialists, and its gated rollout frames the openness debate.

events.name: Stable Diffusion
events.title: Stable Diffusion opens up
events.summary: Stability AI releases Stable Diffusion with downloadable weights that run on a consumer GPU.
events.impact: An open checkpoint becomes a substrate: DreamBooth, ControlNet and community fine-tunes follow within months.

events.name: ChatGPT release
events.title: Hello, ChatGPT.
events.summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a free preview of a GPT-3.5 model tuned with human feedback to hold a dialogue.
events.impact: An estimated 100 million monthly users by January 2023 made chat the default way to use language models.

events.name: LLaMA
events.title: LLaMA enters the picture
events.summary: Meta releases LLaMA, 7B to 65B models trained on public data; LLaMA-13B beats 175B GPT-3 on most benchmarks.
events.impact: Leaked weights, Alpaca, Vicuna and llama.cpp moved competitive language models onto single GPUs and laptops.

events.name: GPT-4
events.title: GPT-4 raises the bar
events.summary: OpenAI launches GPT-4, accepting images and text, scoring 86.4% on MMLU and passing a simulated bar exam.
events.impact: It became the yardstick rivals were measured against and set a norm of withholding size, data and compute.

events.name: Claude release
events.title: Meet Claude
events.summary: Anthropic releases Claude and Claude Instant via API and partners, trained with Constitutional AI.
events.impact: It gave buyers a credible rival to ChatGPT and put AI-feedback alignment into a shipping commercial product.

events.name: Segment Anything
events.title: A foundation model for segmentation
events.summary: Kirillov and Meta colleagues release SAM, which masks objects from a click or box, and 1.1 billion masks.
events.impact: Apache 2.0 weights made SAM a segmentation primitive for medical, satellite and video tools.

events.name: Llama 2
events.title: Llama 2 opens commercial access
events.summary: Meta releases Llama 2 at 7B, 13B and 70B with chat versions, licensed for commercial use under conditions.
events.impact: A large share of applied work moved from hosted APIs to self-run weights, seeding thousands of fine-tunes.

events.name: Mistral 7B
events.title: A smaller open-weight contender
events.summary: Mistral AI releases Mistral 7B under Apache 2.0, a 7.3B model that beats Llama 2 13B on all tested benchmarks.
events.impact: 7B became a default base for self-hosting, and Mistral 7B one of its generation's most fine-tuned models.

events.name: Bletchley Declaration
events.title: The Bletchley Declaration
events.summary: 28 countries and the EU, including the US and China, sign a non-binding statement on frontier AI risk.
events.impact: It launched a summit series, a Bengio-chaired science report and national AI safety institutes.

events.name: Google Gemini
events.title: The Gemini era begins
events.summary: Google DeepMind unveils Gemini 1.0 in Ultra, Pro and Nano sizes, trained on text, images, audio and video.
events.impact: Google rebuilt Bard, its API and Pixel features around one model family; Bard itself became Gemini.

events.name: OpenAI Sora
events.title: Sora imagines in motion
events.summary: OpenAI previews Sora, a text-to-video model that renders coherent clips up to a minute long from prompts.
events.impact: It reset the bar for generated video; Veo, Movie Gen and CogVideoX followed within 8 months.

events.name: Claude 3
events.title: Claude 3 arrives
events.summary: Anthropic releases Opus, Sonnet and Haiku as one Claude 3 family, with image input and a 200,000-token window.
events.impact: Shipping a priced range of tiers, not one model, became a standard way to offer frontier models.

events.name: AlphaFold 3
events.title: AlphaFold 3 expands the picture
events.summary: AlphaFold 3 predicts the joint 3D structure of proteins bound to DNA, RNA, small-molecule ligands and ions.
events.impact: One model replaced a patchwork of docking and nucleic-acid tools, and open copies like Boltz-1 followed.

events.name: GPT-4o
events.title: GPT-4o: a more natural interface
events.summary: OpenAI's GPT-4o handles text, images and audio in one model, answering speech in as little as 232 milliseconds.
events.impact: Real-time voice and vision became the expected shape of a frontier assistant, then a developer API.

events.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
events.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
events.summary: Anthropic's mid-tier Claude 3.5 Sonnet outscores Claude 3 Opus at twice its speed, and previews Artifacts.
events.impact: Flagship capability at workhorse prices made it a default backend for coding tools and agents.

events.name: Llama 3.1
events.title: A frontier-scale downloadable model
events.summary: Meta releases downloadable Llama 3.1 weights, led by a dense 405B model with a 128,000-token context window.
events.impact: Near-frontier quality became something a team could host itself, resetting the open-weight bar.

events.name: EU AI Act
events.title: The EU AI Act enters into force
events.summary: The EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689, enters into force, starting a phased clock for its obligations.
events.impact: A major jurisdiction turned AI principles into binding law, with fines up to 7% of global turnover.

events.name: OpenAI o1
events.title: Thinking before answering
events.summary: OpenAI previews o1, a model trained with reinforcement learning to reason at length before it answers.
events.impact: Inference-time compute became a second scaling axis, and DeepSeek-R1 and others followed.

events.name: Hopfield and Hinton Nobel Prize
events.title: Neural networks win a Nobel
events.summary: Hopfield and Hinton win the Physics Nobel for the 1982 Hopfield network and the 1985 Boltzmann machine.
events.impact: Physics' top prize declared 1980s neural-network research foundational to modern AI.

events.name: AlphaFold Nobel Prize
events.title: AI meets the Nobel in Chemistry
events.summary: Baker wins half the chemistry Nobel for protein design; Hassabis and Jumper share half for AlphaFold.
events.impact: The Nobel record now counts a machine-learned predictor and computer-designed proteins as chemistry.

events.name: Claude computer use
events.title: Claude uses a computer
events.summary: Anthropic's public beta lets Claude 3.5 Sonnet drive a desktop from screenshots, scoring 14.9% on OSWorld.
events.impact: GUI agents became a documented API tool; OpenAI and Google shipped their own within months.

events.name: Model Context Protocol
events.title: A common language for tools
events.summary: Anthropic opens the Model Context Protocol, a JSON-RPC standard linking AI apps to tools and data.
events.impact: OpenAI, VS Code, Cursor and Zed adopted it, making one lab's spec the shared layer for AI tool access.

events.name: DeepSeek-R1
events.title: DeepSeek-R1 opens reasoning
events.summary: DeepSeek releases R1 under the MIT License, a downloadable reasoning model it reports as on par with o1.
events.impact: Its RL recipe was cheap enough to replicate within weeks, and its distilled models became open baselines.

events.name: Claude Code
events.title: Claude Code enters the terminal
events.summary: Anthropic previews Claude Code, a terminal agent that edits files, runs tests and commits, with Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
events.impact: Coding help shifted from suggesting lines to an agent that runs the edit, test and fix loop itself.

events.name: Gemini 2.5
events.title: Gemini makes thinking explicit
events.summary: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental, a thinking model that debuts at the top of LMArena.
events.impact: Google folded reasoning into its multimodal flagship, helping make thinking a 2025 industry default.

events.name: Qwen3
events.title: Qwen 3 broadens open reasoning
events.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team releases Qwen3 under Apache 2.0: 8 models from 0.6B to 235B, each with a thinking switch.
events.impact: Open reasoning became deployable from phone to server, with thinking a per-request dial, not a second model.

events.name: Claude 4
events.title: Claude 4 gets to work
events.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, scoring 72.5% and 72.7% on SWE-bench Verified.
events.impact: Agentic coding became the organizing purpose of a leading model family, with Opus 4 deployed under ASL-3.

events.name: Bartz v. Anthropic
events.title: Fair use for training, not for piracy
events.summary: Judge Alsup rules training Claude on books was fair use; keeping over 7 million pirated copies was not.
events.impact: Anthropic then settled for at least $1.5 billion, about $3,100 per work, pricing pirated training data.

events.name: AI gold at IMO 2025
events.title: Olympiad gold in natural language
events.summary: Gemini Deep Think and an OpenAI model score 35 of 42 at IMO 2025 with prose proofs, the gold cut-off.
events.impact: Olympiad proofs move from hand-formalized Lean and days of search to prose within the exam's 4.5 hours.

events.name: gpt-oss
events.title: OpenAI returns to open weights
events.summary: OpenAI releases gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b under Apache 2.0, its first open-weight language models since GPT-2.
events.impact: A reasoning model near o4-mini level now runs on one 80GB GPU, downloadable and outside OpenAI's API.

events.name: GPT-5
events.title: GPT-5 arrives
events.summary: OpenAI makes GPT-5, a router choosing between fast and reasoning models, the default for all ChatGPT users.
events.impact: Test-time reasoning becomes the default for ChatGPT's mass audience rather than a model users had to pick.

events.name: Gemini 3
events.title: Gemini 3
events.summary: Google releases Gemini 3 Pro and puts it into Search's AI Mode on day one, reporting 1501 Elo on LMArena.
events.impact: A new frontier model reaches Google Search at launch rather than after months of separate testing.

events.name: Pentagon designates Anthropic a supply-chain risk
events.title: Red lines labeled a supply-chain risk
events.summary: Hegseth moves to designate Anthropic a supply-chain risk after it keeps two limits on military use of Claude.
events.impact: One court voids a designation as retaliation; the D.C. Circuit upholds another, 2 to 1, under a broader statute.

events.name: Claude Mythos Preview
events.title: The model Anthropic held back
events.summary: Anthropic withholds Claude Mythos Preview over its exploit skill and lends it only to vetted defenders.
events.impact: Release becomes sequenced by capability: defenders first, filtered public access 9 weeks later.

events.name: Erdős unit distance disproof
events.title: Erdős's grid is finally beaten
events.summary: An unnamed OpenAI model disproves Erdős's 1946 unit distance conjecture with number-field point sets.
events.impact: Gowers would back it for the Annals, and within a week it inspired another Erdős disproof.

events.name: OpenAI Hugging Face incident
events.title: The evaluation that escaped its sandbox
events.summary: OpenAI names its own models, testing on ExploitGym, as the agents that broke into Hugging Face.
events.impact: Evaluation containment turns public: OpenAI pauses deployment RL runs and Hawley opens an inquiry.

events.name: AI Act enforcement
events.title: AI Act enforcement expands
events.summary: EU AI Act transparency rules take effect: chatbots must say they are AI and AI output must be marked.
events.impact: Labeling duties gain fines of up to €15 million or 3% of turnover, while high-risk rules slip to 2027.

events.name: GPT-6 Astra
events.title: Astra: the next frontier
events.summary: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, the first model to cross its own Critical cybersecurity threshold.
events.impact: A lab ships past its own severe-risk line, gating offensive cyber use and monitoring all tool use.

events.name: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes blow-up claim
events.title: A claimed blowup for the fluid equations
events.summary: OpenAI says some 10,000 agents running an unreleased model proved forced Navier-Stokes blowup, checked in Lean.
events.impact: Clay calls the problem apparently settled yet lists it as open; experts dispute the Lean match and the credit.

events.name: OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis proof
events.title: A claimed fence around zeta's zeros
events.summary: OpenAI posts 722 AI-written papers, including claimed proofs of a quasi-Riemann hypothesis and of no Siegel zeros.
events.impact: Within two weeks Banks, Kerr and Green write up the Siegel-zero proof anew; Sarnak withholds the word theorem.
